//fhirclient: fhirclient 3 (2026-09-20) is why there is no `overrides` block here any more,
and why the Client TYPE is declared in packages/core/src/types/smartClient.ts
instead of imported. Read that file's header before touching either.
WHY THE UPGRADE. v2 reached crypto through isomorphic-webcrypto, which dragged
in react-native-securerandom and therefore react-native itself — and 14 of the
root lockfile's 30 advisories, including the only CRITICAL one (shell-quote,
via metro). None of it was code the bundle shipped: fhirclient's browser entry
reached isomorphic-webcrypto only through `globalThis.crypto ? globalThis.crypto
: require('isomorphic-webcrypto')`, a require inside a ternary that a browser
never evaluates and Rollup never statically bundles. An `expo-random: 11.0.0`
override pruned the Expo half; the react-native half survived every pin,
because react-native-securerandom declares a hard `react-native: "*"` peer in
every published version. v3 depends on `jose` and `js-base64` and nothing else.
Measured: 30 -> 21 advisories (0 critical), node_modules 438M -> 248M, lockfile
895 -> 548 packages, and the override deleted.
⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHY THE LOCAL TYPE. fhirclient 3.0.0's published tarball
OMITS `types/types.d.ts`, while every one of its shipped declarations opens
with `import { fhirclient } from "./types"`. `skipLibCheck: true` swallows the
TS2307, so nothing goes red — the types just degrade. Measured on this tree:
`client.state` became `any`, `client.request`'s parameters became `any`, and a
type-aware lint probe went from 34 unsafe flows in production code to 43. With
the five-member surface we declare ourselves it is 28 — better than v2 ever
was, because `request`'s two call shapes are now named.
⚠️ Do not treat any count here as current — re-run `npm audit` and reclassify
with `npm explain <pkg>` before citing one.
